status: PROVISIONAL — physically reasoned, NOT empirically fitted
domain: gamma-encoded sRGB 8-bit medians (the same domain the DPD constant lives in)
model: total chlorine mg/L = k_oto_srgb * log10(B_white / B_sample) * dilution
why_not_fitted: No standard and no classical source publishes an absorbance-per-mg/L or a molar
absorptivity for the o-tolidine yellow holoquinone. JIS K 0106:2010 Annex A,
IS 3025 (Part 26):1986, the Standard Methods lineage and every field kit all say the
same thing: construct a calibration curve. Four researchers searched independently and
none found a primary measurement. So this constant is a reasoned prior, not a fit.
Replace it using fit_oto_calibration.py before OTO mode leaves beta.

derivation.method: ratio to the shipped DPD constant, so every term that belongs to the photographic pipeline rather than to the dye (sRGB gamma, effective vial path length, exposure, illuminant, white-card geometry) cancels exactly
derivation.formula: k_OTO = k_DPD * (eta_DPD * n_DPD * eps_DPD) / (eta_OTO * n_OTO * eps_OTO)
derivation.k_dpd_check: refit through origin from the six Chlor-Test card points: sum(A*c)/sum(A^2) = 0.516018/0.136583 = 3.7781 — confirms the shipped constant exactly
derivation.eps_dpd: 19930 M^-1 cm^-1 at 510 nm (Wurster radical cation; Bader, Sturzenegger & Hoigne, Water Research 22:1109, 1988)
derivation.n_dpd: 2 — HOCl is a 2-electron oxidant, the Wurster cation a 1-electron product, so 1 Cl2 makes 2 chromophores
derivation.eps_oto: 5.0e4 M^-1 cm^-1 at 438 nm — INFERRED, the load-bearing weakness. Scaled from TMB's diimine (same benzidine-diimine chromophore) eps_450 = 5.9e4 (Josephy, Eling & Mason, J. Biol. Chem. 257:3669, 1982), corrected down for weaker methyl donation and up ~1.4x for strong-acid enhancement. Honest bracket 3.5-7.0e4.
derivation.n_oto: 1 — o-tolidine to holoquinone is a 2-electron/2-proton change against a 2-electron oxidant
derivation.eta_note: band-overlap efficiency from a spectral forward model over the Jiang et al. (2013) 28-camera sensitivity database. DPD's 510/553 nm double band sits under the CENTRE of the green channel; OTO's 438 nm peak sits 22 nm BELOW the blue channel's 460 nm peak, on its 421 nm half-power shoulder.
derivation.coincidence_warning: The near-equality with DPD's 3.778 is genuine, not a copy-paste bug: OTO's larger eps is almost exactly cancelled by its 1:1 rather than 2:1 stoichiometry and its worse blue-channel overlap. Do not 'fix' it.

corroboration: Independent spectral forward model (28 cameras x dye band x sRGB encode), which first reproduced k_DPD as 3.844 (1.7% error, R^2 0.997) before being pointed at OTO: 4.03 median camera, 4.32 +/- 0.61 mean
Beer-Lambert from scratch: 4.02 once the band-overlap factor is corrected from an assumed 0.9 to the measured 0.776

range.floor_rationale: Measured against the app own yellow detector: below about 0.22 mg/L the OTO yellow is too faint for a camera to separate from white paper (it fails the (R-B)>30 test), so the app REFUSES rather than guessing. The synthesis proposed a 0.1-0.2 semi-quantitative band; that is achievable by eye against a comparator disc but NOT by this method, and claiming it would invite a fabricated reading at the exact concentration where a false pass is most dangerous. The floor and the quantitative lower bound coincide at ~0.2 mg/L, which is convenient but not engineered.
range.gate_rationale: Gate on TRANSMITTANCE (sample/reference), not on the raw channel code and not on computed mg/L. Not mg/L, because the concentration at which the response flattens depends on absorptivity and path length, neither of which the app knows. Not the raw code either: an absolute floor of 125 fires at 0.32 mg/L against a dim reference and 1.24 mg/L against a bright one, a 4x swing driven purely by exposure. Saturation is a ratio phenomenon, so the gate must be a ratio. T = 0.56 is where the +/-15% accuracy ceiling lands across a wide sweep of absorptivity and path length; at k=4.0 it corresponds to 4.0*log10(1/0.56) = 1.01 mg/L.
range.gate_implied_ceiling: At k=4.0 and B_white=223 the gate fires at 4.0*log10(223/125) = 1.005 mg/L. The app derives the published lower bound from the gate and the actual white reference of each photo, so the two can never drift apart.

why_it_saturates.summary: The blue channel does NOT bottom out at 0. It PLATEAUS, and a linear model built on it UNDER-REPORTS — the dangerous direction.
why_it_saturates.mechanism: 17.1% of the blue channel's response (7.5-31.7% across cameras, 30.4% for the one phone sensor) lies where the 438 nm holoquinone absorbs under 10% of its peak. That unabsorbed leak acts as a stray-light floor: simulated blue code at 10 mg/L is 66-119, never near 0.
why_it_saturates.not_gamma: Proven spectral, not gamma: the same simulation in the linear domain with no gamma gives -34.4% at 2 mg/L vs -33.5% gamma-encoded. Linearising does not fix it.
why_it_saturates.do_not_reuse: poolcheck.js RELIABLE_MAX = 3.0 is well beyond the OTO asymptote and must not be carried over.

gamma.detail: sRGB is a near-exact power law, so a ratio of encoded values is the encoded ratio: A_app = A_true/gamma_eff, with gamma_eff constant within 2% (2.254 at A=0.05, 2.208 at A=0.6) from code 255 down to ~119. Gamma rescales k by ~2.2 and does not bend the line.
gamma.toe: gamma_eff falls to 2.10 at code 100, 1.41 at 20, 1.0 below 10. The blue-code gate at 125 keeps the app out of the toe.
gamma.if_you_ever_linearise: k would become 4.0/2.21 = 1.8. Shipping 4.0 against linearised values would over-report by 2.2x. Ship exactly one domain; never a runtime toggle.
gamma.identifiability: An earlier draft claimed sRGB's 2.2 was 'recovered from your own photographs' because A_true/A_app = 0.562/0.2647 = 2.12. That is degenerate and has been removed. The quantity actually recovered is gamma/(eta_DPD * L_eff), which lands near 2.2 only because eta_DPD*L_eff = 0.706*1.47 happens to be ~1.04. Using the same eta with L = 1 cm the identical calculation 'recovers' 1.50. gamma, eta_DPD and L_eff are mutually unidentifiable from the card data. They cancel only in the ratio - which is the real reason to prefer the ratio, and is unaffected by dropping the claim.

geometry_warning: Valid only at the optical geometry of the DPD calibration (a printed comparator card photographed the same way). Scale by (L_calibration / L_user) for a different vial: Lovibond's Comparator 2000+ cell is 13.5 mm, a Nessler tube 113 mm — an 8.4x error between them.

chemistry_gates.acid_variant_only: This implements the classical ACID o-tolidine test (final pH 1-3), product = yellow holoquinone, lambda-max 435-440 nm. IS 3025 (Part 26):1986 codifies the STABILIZED NEUTRAL variant (pH 6.5-7.5) whose product is the BLUE meriquinone read at 625 nm — a blue-channel model reads near-zero on it and would report 'safe'.
chemistry_gates.hue_gate: Compute absorbance in all three channels. Refuse when red absorbance is a meaningful fraction of blue: blue-green means under-acidified/expired/neutral reagent, orange-brown means over-oxidation by excess chlorine. Only a clean yellow is on the calibration.

known_biases: OTO reads low against reference methods even with perfect optics: ~90% of true for hypochlorite and inorganic chloramines, ~50% for organic chloramines and real chlorinated pool water
Nitrite false positive: 0.2 mg/L NO2-N fakes 0.03-0.05 mg/L chlorine over an hour
Iron(III) at long reaction times, and manganese, which no reagent modification fixes
Turbidity and raw-water colour, which the app cannot blank out the way the classical orthotolidine-arsenite procedure did
Cross-camera scatter in the constant is ~14%, roughly double DPD's ~8%
Sample should be below 20 C; precision degrades as temperature rises

reaction_time.note: Acid OTO read at under ~15 s approximates FREE chlorine; read at 5 min it is TOTAL. JIS restricts reading to 10 min because the colour keeps rising (still climbing hours later). A photo with no timing discipline measures neither quantity cleanly, which is why the app records elapsed time and says so when it was not recorded.

acceptance_test.note: Real photographs should sit ABOVE these at the top end — that is the spectral leak. Landing far off at the LOW end means eps or the acid regime is wrong.

next_steps_by_value: One UV-Vis scan, 400-700 nm, of a 1.00 mg/L chlorine standard developed with the actual reagent in the actual vial. Pins eps, band FWHM and any meriquinone contamination at once, collapsing +/-40% to a few percent.
Empirical refit with fit_oto_calibration.py against a printed chloroscope card (closer optical analogue than Lovibond's coloured GLASS filters), fitting 0.15-1.25 mg/L only and extrapolating nothing.
Only then, the 2-parameter leak-corrected model on linearised values, which cut max error over 1-3 mg/L from ~49% to under 10% in simulation.

corroboration_CORRECTED.claim_withdrawn: An earlier draft claimed three independently converging routes (3.88-4.09, 4.03, 4.02). Adversarial review showed that is overstated and it has been withdrawn.
corroboration_CORRECTED.what_actually_holds: ONE physical route: the ratio to the DPD fit. The other two are not independent of it.
corroboration_CORRECTED.route_2_not_independent: The 28-camera forward model 'reproducing k_DPD as 3.844' required assuming the same effective path length the anchor already carries. It is the anchor re-expressed, not a check on it.
corroboration_CORRECTED.route_3_arithmetic_error: The from-scratch Beer-Lambert route was reported as landing on 4.02 after 'correcting f to the measured 0.776'. That substitutes a RATIO where an ABSOLUTE belongs: in k = gamma/(eps*n*L*1.4103e-5*eta_OTO) the divisor is eta_OTO = 0.548, not eta_OTO/eta_DPD = 0.776. Executed correctly with the same inputs it gives 5.7, not 4.02. It appeared to agree only because the erroneous 0.776/0.548 = 1.416 stood in for a path length the route had omitted.
corroboration_CORRECTED.implied_path_length: Backing L out of the anchor gives L_eff = 2.2/(3.778*1.4103e-5*0.706*2*19930) = 1.47 cm. This is NOT a measured bore; it is the effective path length implied by the Chlor-Test card fit. Any different vial must rescale k by L_calibration/L_user.

adversarial_review.verdict: All three reviewers refuted the proposal as first stated. None asked for a different value of k; all three attacked the envelope around it. The changes below were made in response.
adversarial_review.fatal_finding_fixed: SEGMENTATION WAS CONFOUNDED WITH THE MEASURED AXIS. Selecting 'sample' pixels by a yellow hue test is selecting on the illuminant colour-temperature axis itself: under a warm cast, white card pixels satisfy the yellow test, join the sample population and drag its median onto the card. Simulation showed the reading FREEZING at ~0.18 mg/L across a true 0.30-0.75 mg/L range at a 20-code cast, with every quality gate still passing and the hue gate manufacturing the very A_B > A_G > A_R ordering it looks for. FIX: the reference is now chosen by brightness in the measuring channel alone (a chroma-free criterion), the frame is white-balanced by it, and the hue tests run on normalised values, making them cast-invariant.
adversarial_review.gate_moved_to_transmittance: The absolute blue-code gate at 125 was refuted as exposure-dependent: across the white levels the app already accepts it fires anywhere from 0.32 to 1.24 mg/L, a 4x swing. Saturation is a ratio phenomenon, so the gate is now on transmittance, sample/reference <= 0.56.
adversarial_review.uncertainty_now_published: The +/-40% bracket straddles the 0.2 mg/L adequacy threshold in BOTH directions - at the low end of the bracket a true 0.15 mg/L would display as 0.21 and appear to clear a line it does not clear. Every OTO reading is therefore published as an interval, never a bare number.
adversarial_review.pool_warning_added: The most dangerous real pool reads high on total chlorine and zero on free, all of it bound as chloramine; it smells strongly of chlorine and is not disinfected. OTO cannot distinguish it from a sanitized pool. Pool mode now names that failure explicitly.
adversarial_review.clipped_reference_rejected: A blown-out white card has lost its own value to saturation, so every ratio against it reads LOW. Now refused.

OPEN - not fixed in v1.no_sample_blank: The strongest remaining objection. Iron(III), tannin/humic colour and turbidity all attenuate blue preferentially, so they PASS the hue gate as legitimate yellow and can fabricate roughly 0.05-0.2 mg/L of apparent total chlorine on chlorine-free water - straddling the decision threshold, in exactly the raw handpump water a PHED/JJM user is testing. The classical orthotolidine-arsenite procedure blanked this out; this app cannot. The fix is a paired photograph of the same vial BEFORE reagent development, with A = log10(B_blank/B_developed), which also removes the vial and geometry terms. Deferred to v2 because it changes the capture workflow.
OPEN - not fixed in v1.isp_colour_matrix: Phone JPEG pipelines apply a 3x3 colour-correction matrix with large negative off-diagonals. For a neutral card the off-diagonals cancel; for a saturated yellow they do not, and the blue row is typically the most aggressive. This does not cancel in the DPD-to-OTO ratio and is not bounded by the +/-40% bracket, so the stated ~14% cross-camera scatter is an underestimate of unknown size.
OPEN - not fixed in v1.temperature: The classical method wants sample below 20 C, which is unsatisfiable in 30-35 C Indian surface water. The app records temperature but does not gate on it.
